title: Victoria Hamilton in Albion - Almeida Theatre - BBC4 - review
transcript: hello and welcome to one minute theater reviews i'm paul seven lewis and today i'm going to be reviewing mike bartlett's albion directed by rupert gould and recorded live at the almeida theatre in london currently available on bbc iplayer sometimes when you watch the first act of a play and it's all the setup and you really want to get it over with and move on to the good stuff but in the case of albion the first act really is the best audrey has bought a house that she knew as a child it had an historic garden and she plans to renovate it no matter that this involves uprooting her daughter neglecting her business upsetting the local community who've become used to using the huge outdoor space for their annual events it's a good script but what you're riveted by is victoria hamilton's performance from the start she grabs you by the lapels she's mesmerizing as she paces back and forth and spits out her staccato sentences like a neurotic sergeant major let me be mother seeing as i am this is the sort of intimate theater that works really well in a live recording the almeida is a small theater and the casts are on a three-sided stage so it's like an oval island surrounded by the audience well actually it's not an island it's a garden with a solid tree at one end which i think gives a sense of history the actors don't have to shout and the cameras can close in on a face much as you would if you were lucky enough to be sitting in one of the seats that's my one minute review keep watching for more of my thoughts on albion at the almeida now available on bbc iplayer so for me nothing lived up to that first act but as it continues there's a lot going on with developments involving other characters they felt tacked on no matter how good the acting was it wasn't so much multi-layered as laid on thick and the ending was well way too melodramatic what i loved throughout the whole play was this dominating character of audrey grief has consumed her and the only way she can cope is to reject everyone and everything in favor of a retreat into an imagined golden age she has lost her soldier's son in what she sees as defending his country but what is referred to at one point as a folly as a way of honoring him she's determined to recreate the original garden even though it's now anachronistic it's pointed out that the climate has changed and in this context climate may refer to more than growing conditions because there is an allegory here for the state of england of how we as a nation are coping with the loss of a mythical past glory uh and with the need to move on audrey wants to return to a bygone age but only within the boundaries of her world so she doesn't care that she's trampling on the traditions of the local people and that she hires the more efficient polish cleaner and sacks the local woman who's done the job for 20 years it's fascinating shocking even to see the insensitivity that can come from single-mindedness and to see her gradual but inevitable disintegration it's also fascinating to see the garden change as flowers grow through the four acts each of which is a different season culminating with the fall it's a great design by miriam buter i glossed over the other characters early but that doesn't mean i didn't think they were good or all that they weren't acted well audrey's daughter zara is played by daisy edgar jones who recently made a breakthrough to stardom with her role in tv's normal people she's perfect as her troubled 20-something then helen schlesinger makes you feel the pain as this successful but shy novelist forced to make a hard choice between a 30-year friendship and a rare opportunity for love in a play that is more amusing than funny nicholas rowe as audrey's devoted husband got the most laughs as a man so proudly laid back that he was almost horizontal for me one of the tests of watching theater at home is whether i wish i'd seen it in the theater and in albion's case despite some flaws i would have loved to have been there especially to see that outstanding performance by victoria hamilton i give albion four stars if you found this review useful please subscribe to my youtube channel one minute theater reviews by pressing the button somewhere below and if you can't get enough of me please visit my website one minute theater reviews dot co dot uk or listen to my program on stage musicals on box office radio dot co dot uk mondays at 7 pm thank you for watching you
